COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
 
AO No.73 of 2021
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. H.C. Pande, Advocate for the appellant.
Instant appeal is preferred against the 
judgment and award dated 22.01.2021, passed in 
Motor Accident Claim No.288 of 2017, Smt. Swarn 
Kaur and others vs. Devendra Pal Singh and another, 
by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Additional 
District Judge, Khatima, District Udham Singh 
Nagar.
Heard.
Admit.
Issue notices to the respondents. 
Summon the LCR.
Heard on Stay Application (IA) No.1 of 2021.
Learned counsel for the appellant would 
submit that it is a case filed under collusion; the 
vehicle which according to the claimants hits the 
deceased has falsely been planted to get the 
insurance; FIR was lodged after 27 days; there is no 
medical prescriptions which may reveal that the 
death was by accident, even the postmortem does not 
reveal that it was a case of road accident. 
Be it as it may, this Court does not see any 
reason to stay the operation of the judgment and 
award. Appellant shall deposit the amount, which 
shall be invested in a recurring term deposit in some 
nationalized bank. The amount shall not be released 
without prior permission of this Court. 
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 09.04.2021
Sanjay

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
IA No.02 of 2021 (Money Withdrawal Application)
In
AO No.73 of 2021
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via video conferencing).
Mr. H.C. Pande, Advocate, for the 
appellant.
Mr. Pradeep Chamyal, Advocate, for the 
respondent. 
As a result of the accident, which has 
chanced on 13.08.2017, the husband of the 
respondent No.1, Late Mr. Jaswant Singh, has 
met with the sad demise. On the culmination of 
the proceeding of MACP Case No.288 of 2017, 
which was rendered by an award dated 
22.01.2021, the total amount of compensation, 
which has been determined to be paid was on 
the basis of the salary drawn by the 
deceased/Jaswant Singh, who was of 53 years 
of age, at that relevant point of time, working as 
an Assistant Teacher. The compensation was 
assessed to be made payable to the tune of 
Rs.68,07,005/-.
This Court while admitting the appeal 
from order on 09.04.2021, had directed the 
appellant to deposit the entire amount, before 
the MACT concerned, and the same has been  deposited in compliance thereto, along with an 
interest.
Today the matter is listed on the money 
withdrawal application.
Considering the fact that the widow and 
the children i.e. respondent Nos.1, 2 and 3 
herein, in order to sustain themselves in life
after the death of the only breadwinner, it 
would be in the interest of justice that 25% of 
the total awarded amount i.e. Rs.68,07,005/-, is 
permitted to be withdrawn by the respondent 
No.1, herein.
Accordingly, the money withdrawal 
application would stand disposed of with a 
direction to the MACT Tribunal/Additional 
District Judge, Khatima, District Udham Singh 
Nagar, before whom the money stands 
deposited, to remit the 25% of the awarded 
amount to the respondent No.1 to 3, herein, 
within a period of six weeks from the date of 
the presentation of the certified copy of this 
judgment. 
Accordingly, the money withdrawal 
application stands disposed of.
List this appeal from order in the last 
week of September, 2021.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 13.08.2021
NR/

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
AO No.73 of 2021
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
Mr. Pulak Aggarwal, learned counsel for 
the appellant.
2. Mr. Pradeep Chamyal, learned counsel for 
respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants.
3. Earlier money withdrawal application on 
behalf of respondent nos.1 to 3 was filed and 
vide order dated 13.08.2021 Co-ordinate 
Bench had directed the MACT to release 25% 
of the total awarded amount i.e. 68,07,005/- in 
favour of respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants.
4. Now, respondent nos.1 to 3/ claimants 
have filed Money Withdrawal Application 
(IA/3/2024) praying for release of the 
remaining amount.
5. It is stated in the accompanying affidavit
to the money withdrawal application filed by 
respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants that 
respondent nos.1, 2 and 3 are wife, daughter 
and son of the deceased respectively; 
respondent no.1 is more than 54 years old lady 
and she is suffering from various old age 
diseases and her regular treatment is going on; 
the claimants/ respondents are suffering from 
financial crises, who are unable to maintain 
themselves and they are in dire need of money 
for their livelihood, hence, they may be  permitted to withdraw the entire amount 
deposited before the learned Tribunal. 
6. No objection has been filed to the Money 
Withdrawal Application, however, learned 
counsel for the appellant orally opposes the 
money withdrawal application.
7. Considering the facts and circumstances 
of the case that have been brought on record, 
Money Withdrawal Application is allowed and 
additional 25% out of the total remaining 
amount i.e. the amount remaining after 
withdrawal of earlier 25% amount from 
₹68,07,005/- deposited by the appellant before 
the Tribunal is ordered to be released in favour 
of respondent nos.1 to 3/ claimants, as per 
their respective share, within three weeks from 
the date of presentation of the certified copy of 
this order.
8. List on 17.10.2025.
9. Misc. Application (IA/5/2025) stands 
disposed of.
 (Subhash Upadhyay,J.)
 07.08.2025
SS
